subject.title: fix(agent): duplicate same-session turn when the gateway connection drops after accepting a run

question: Should the accepted-disconnect path land now as a fresh-session recook fallback, or wait for the broader reattach-first recovery design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98200?
rationale: The patch fixes the same-session transcript collision, but it intentionally preserves a two-execution fallback boundary for accepted disconnects, which affects session ownership and possible message delivery side effects.

options.title: Land focused fix now
options.body: Accept the existing timeout-style two-run fallback boundary for this edge case and merge the narrow same-session protection after refreshed exact-head checks.

options.title: Pause for reattach-first design
options.body: Hold this PR and decide the broader wait/reattach behavior first if duplicate model/tool execution is not acceptable for accepted disconnects.

options.title: Split delivery-sensitive behavior
options.body: Ask for a narrower follow-up that treats `--deliver` differently if maintainers want to reduce double-send risk before accepting the interactive fallback behavior.

recommendation.title: Land focused fix now
recommendation.body: Accept the existing timeout-style two-run fallback boundary for this edge case and merge the narrow same-session protection after refreshed exact-head checks.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent gateway/session work makes this the best available routing owner for the session-state fallback tradeoff, though ownership is shared with gateway transport contributors.
